entities.summary:
Stratonice of Cappadocia was a princess of the Seleucid Empire, born to Antiochus II Theos and Laodice I around 280 BCE. As a member of the royal family, she was involved in the politics and intrigues of the Seleucid court.

Stratonice was known for her diplomatic skills and her ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Seleucid kings and their neighbors. Her brother Seleucus II Callinicus succeeded their father as king and went on to face challenges from the Ptolemaic Kingdom and the Parthian Empire.

Stratonice's legacy is tied to the rise of the Seleucid Empire, which played a significant role in the Hellenistic period and had a lasting impact on the ancient world. Her story is also linked to the cultural and religious developments of the time, including the spread of Greek culture and the influence of Zoroastrianism.

In the end, Stratonice's life was cut short, and her fate remains a mystery. Despite this, her significance as a princess of the Seleucid Empire and her role in shaping the course of history cannot be overstated.
